events.title: Death of the Prophet Muhammad
events.description: Muhammad, the central figure of Islam, died in Medina. He had united much of the Arabian Peninsula under a new faith in his final years.
events.significance: His death opened the question of leadership of the Muslim community. That led to the era of the caliphs and the rapid expansion of the Islamic world.

events.title: Vikings raid Lindisfarne
events.description: Norse raiders attacked the monastery on Lindisfarne, an island off the coast of Northumbria in England. They plundered the abbey and shocked Christian Europe.
events.significance: The raid is commonly accepted as the start of Norse activity in the British Isles. It marks the beginning of the Viking Age.

events.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four is published in the United States
events.description: George Orwell's dystopian novel appeared in American bookstores. It imagines a world of total surveillance, propaganda and rewritten history.
events.significance: The book gave us terms such as Big Brother and Orwellian. It remains a touchstone in debates about privacy, truth and state power.

events.title: James Earl Ray arrested in London
events.description: Two months after the assassination of Martin Luther King Jr., Ray was arrested at Heathrow Airport in London. He was traveling on a false passport.
events.significance: The arrest ended one of the largest international manhunts of its time. Ray was extradited to the United States and prosecuted for King's murder.
